title: From the Editor — The Edge of the Map
settingText: RFV Glass Horizon hangs small against the immense Aurin Rift: crystalline asteroid fragments catch cold light while a dark unmarked corridor opens beyond them. The ship reads as a working Fleet survey cruiser with sensor booms, small-craft bays and a fractured-crystal crest. No threat, battle or spoiler imagery; the dominant feeling is scale and unanswered space.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Rex Fleet: Glass Horizon Issue 1. Introduce a series about the moment before unknown space becomes trusted infrastructure.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Glass Horizon should be visually small against the unresolved volume around it. Reserve a calm readable field for the editorial text; do not turn the page into an infographic or ship cutaway.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons. Strong heading, readable body copy, generous spacing, and no invented logos, signage, credits or scientific labels.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Most maps are so useful that we forget what they really are.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone measured the distance. Someone checked the beacon. Someone decided the line was safe enough that people who would never meet them could cross it at speed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: REX FLEET: GLASS HORIZON begins before that promise exists.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Its crew goes where the Fleet still has questions: damaged corridors, strange measurements, anomaly weather, lost signals, and places that may become roads only after somebody is willing to admit how little they know.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This is not the ship that decides what civilization should do.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It is the ship that finds out what reality will allow.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They have found a quiet route.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they have to decide whether it is actually a route at all.

directionInline.text: Interior editorial/interstitial comic page, not a cover. Preserve mature Rex Fleet blue/gold/Ion White language with restrained survey-violet instrumentation.
Do not visually reveal the later beacon-feedback failure or rescue. The page should sell uncertainty and discovery, not the solution.

title: Do Not Call It a Route
summary: Glass Horizon finds an unnaturally calm opening through the Aurin Rift. Six probe returns agree, but Rhea refuses to let early consistency become premature certainty.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE EXTERIOR. Glass Horizon holds position among crystalline Aurin debris; far ahead, a narrow dark gap looks almost too clean compared with the fractured region around it.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM on Mira at navigation with six matching probe tracks layered over one another.
Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT Olan and Anik studying the low-noise trace from independent instruments.
Panel 4 — MEDIUM on Pia at the route table, one finger hovering over the control that would convert the candidate line into a formal map object.
Panel 5 — CLOSE on Rhea, calm rather than dramatic, stopping the language before she stops the work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Six passes. Same entry, same exit, same transit time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: That is better agreement than half the lanes we inherited.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: I can mark a provisional route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Do not call it a route yet.

title: Something Expensive
summary: The team prepares a heavier instrumented probe and Lantern Two. Anik defines the difference between proving a corridor exists and proving it can support real use.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE in the survey hangar. Lantern Two sits beside racks of disposable probes and folded temporary beacons.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM Kess checking the cutter's physical controls while Mira clips in an independent inertial recorder.
Panel 3 — CLOSE Anik swapping a cheap probe package for a heavier instrument pallet.
Panel 4 — TWO-SHOT Olan and Kess beside the cutter canopy.
Panel 5 — INSERT on the heavy probe rolling toward launch, visibly more substantial than the earlier disposable units.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: You said the opening is stable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: I said six cheap things survived it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: A route is what happens after you send something expensive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: I appreciate knowing where I sit in the budget.

title: Too Quiet
summary: The heavy probe returns clean, but the team notices that the candidate corridor contains less background variation than a truly empty reference volume should.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE lab view with the heavy probe's trace over three independent reference traces.
Panel 2 — CLOSE on a flat, nearly featureless noise spectrum.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM Olan leaning in, pleased for half a second.
Panel 4 — CLOSE Anik pointing to the reference baseline beneath the candidate trace.
Panel 5 — THREE-SHOT as the excitement turns into a new question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: No shear spike. No timing scatter. Nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Empty space still has measurement noise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: And this is quieter than the reference volume.

title: Provisional
summary: Pia records the candidate without certifying it. The route exists on the internal survey map as a qualified observation, while its public beacon status remains non-green.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — OVERHEAD on the route table: established green lanes skirt the Aurin debris; the candidate appears only as a thin violet dotted observation line.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM Pia locking the public route layer while preserving the raw survey layer.
Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT Mira and Rhea reviewing the distinction.
Panel 4 — INSERT on a public-beacon control still firmly red/non-certified.
Panel 5 — WIDE through the cartography bay window toward the dark candidate opening outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: Internal observation only. No public route number.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Anyone outside us can see it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: They can see there is survey activity. They cannot see a safe lane.

title: Markers
summary: Glass Horizon deploys temporary survey beacons along the candidate corridor, keeping their public channel non-certified while creating a repeatable instrument baseline.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — EXTERIOR WIDE. Rugged survey beacons unfold from launch canisters around the corridor entry, diagnostic violet against the dark.
Panel 2 — INSIDE LANTERN TWO. Kess flies the outer spacing pattern while Mira calls distance.
Panel 3 — CLOSE on Anik's remote systems display as all six clocks synchronize.
Panel 4 — EXTERIOR DETAIL on one beacon: survey diagnostics active, public navigation face still red/non-certified.
Panel 5 — WIDE showing the complete six-beacon chain disappearing into the calm opening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Beacon Three, two hundred meters starboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: All clocks independent. Public channel stays red.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: You really do not trust this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: I trust it enough to measure it.

title: Three Milliseconds
summary: A beaconed probe returns three milliseconds earlier than the synchronized inertial model predicts. The discrepancy is tiny, repeatable and shared by no other clock aboard ship.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM on Mira freezing a transit trace.
Panel 2 — INSERT: two aligned timing bars ending three milliseconds apart.
Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT Olan and Anik checking independent references rather than arguing from one display.
Panel 4 — CLOSE Rhea listening.
Panel 5 — WIDE bridge as a second heavy probe is already moved toward launch outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: It came back three milliseconds early.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: Early compared with the beacon clocks?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Compared with everything except the corridor.

title: Better Every Time
summary: Repeated passes make the corridor appear progressively cleaner. The result looks like improving stability until Pia notices that the improvement begins only after the temporary beacon chain was activated.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE lab plot showing transit one through transit five, each visibly less noisy.
Panel 2 — CLOSE Olan, openly excited by the pattern.
Panel 3 — Pia reaches across and hides the post-beacon runs, leaving the earlier data visible.
Panel 4 — INSERT on the timeline: beacon activation sits exactly at the change point.
Panel 5 — FOUR-SHOT as everyone understands that the instrument setup may have changed the thing under study.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: Or we are getting better at seeing it.

title: The Instrument Is in the Experiment
summary: Olan and Anik develop the central hypothesis: synchronized beacons may be damping local corridor variation. Rhea accepts the hypothesis only as something to test.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM Olan overlays beacon phase with corridor noise.
Panel 2 — CLOSE Anik highlighting an inverse relationship between correction pulses and measured variation.
Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT; Olan sees the engineering possibility, Anik sees the contamination problem.
Panel 4 — MEDIUM Rhea arrives at the lab rail.
Panel 5 — CLOSE on the trace as another correction pulse flattens a spike.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: The clocks are phase-locking the local fold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: But then we are not just measuring it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Do not fall in love with it first.

title: Lantern Two
summary: Kess and Mira take Lantern Two into the candidate corridor under strict abort limits while Glass Horizon watches from outside.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE hangar launch: Lantern Two drops cleanly from Glass Horizon toward the beacon chain.
Panel 2 — TWO-SHOT cockpit, Kess at pilot and Mira at navigation, both physically tethered into their seats.
Panel 3 — COMMS inset with Rhea on the cutter display.
Panel 4 — EXTERIOR as Lantern Two crosses the first beacon into the unusually calm dark.
Panel 5 — COCKPIT view; the stars ahead look almost ordinary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: One discrepancy outside limits and you come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: No heroics. I found that line in the brief.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: I keep adding it for you.

title: Two Distances
summary: Inside the corridor, optical and active ranging agree with each other but disagree with Lantern Two's inertial displacement. Mira refuses to collapse the contradiction into one convenient answer.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE through the cutter canopy: Beacon Four appears close against an otherwise sparse star field.
Panel 2 — INSERT on range display: optical/active range and inertial displacement differ materially.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM Mira checks the isolated inertial recorder physically rather than trusting the shared bus.
Panel 4 — CLOSE Kess looking from instruments to the apparent beacon.
Panel 5 — TWO-SHOT as Kess flies the inertial instruction instead of the visible line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: They disagree. That is the information.

title: Sight Is Decoration
summary: Visual perspective makes the next beacon appear to drift toward Lantern Two while signal time says it is receding. Mira holds the cutter to inertial history.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — COCKPIT POV: Beacon Five appears larger and visually nearer without the cutter accelerating.
Panel 2 — INSERT: signal time-of-flight lengthens despite the apparent approach.
Panel 3 — CLOSE Kess instinctively beginning to correct toward what she sees.
Panel 4 — Mira's hand stops the correction at the control rail, not dramatically, just immediately.
Panel 5 — WIDE external showing Lantern Two maintaining a clean vector while the apparent geometry shifts around it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Signal says it is moving away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Sight is decoration until the measurements agree.

title: Correction Load
summary: While Lantern Two crosses the corridor, Anik discovers that every beacon is consuming more correction power even though Glass Horizon has not increased its command output.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — CLOSE on six beacon load traces climbing in sequence as the cutter passes them.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM Anik opens the raw hardware telemetry.
Panel 3 — Olan compares the rising load to the still-flattening corridor noise.
Panel 4 — Rhea looks toward the bridge feed showing Lantern Two mid-route.
Panel 5 — INSERT on Beacon Four taking a sharp step upward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: But our commanded field is unchanged.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Is the corridor drawing the difference?

title: One Beacon Dark
summary: The team switches one beacon off. Local noise immediately returns around its segment, supporting the phase-coupling hypothesis and making an engineered route seem briefly possible.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — EXTERIOR: Beacon Two goes dark while the others remain diagnostically violet.
Panel 2 — LAB TRACE: corridor variation rises only around the dark segment.
Panel 3 — Olan cannot hide a small smile at the clean experiment.
Panel 4 — Pia is already thinking about what a maintained beacon chain would mean.
Panel 5 — Rhea keeps the result inside test language.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: Noise is back at Two. Adjacent segments unchanged.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: We are holding the corridor quiet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: If it scales, this is infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Test the sentence before you publish it.

title: Green Is a Promise
summary: The apparent success creates pressure to imagine the route's value. Pia and Rhea deliberately keep public certification locked while authorizing one controlled full-chain transit.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — ROUTE TABLE showing how much distance the candidate could save between existing lanes.
Panel 2 — MEDIUM Olan indicating the projected logistics benefit without overselling it.
Panel 3 — CLOSE Pia's hand above the green-certification control, then moving away from it.
Panel 4 — TWO-SHOT Rhea and Pia.
Panel 5 — WIDE as the map remains violet/provisional.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: It cuts eleven hours from the Aurin crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: Which means miners will use it the hour we mark it green.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Then we do not mark it green.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Green is a promise. We have not earned it.

title: Full Chain
summary: With all six beacons synchronized, Lantern Two begins a complete transit. For several minutes the route performs almost perfectly while the hidden correction load continues climbing.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — SPECTACULAR WIDE. All six survey beacons define a clean path into the quiet corridor; none are green.
Panel 2 — COCKPIT: Kess and Mira see matching inertial and range data for the first time.
Panel 3 — LAB: Olan watches noise collapse toward a stable band.
Panel 4 — SYSTEMS: Anik watches correction load climb above the previous pass.
Panel 5 — SPLIT FEEL without literal infographic: the beauty of the stable path contrasted with Anik's worried hardware trace.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: Nine point four. Nine point four. They finally agree.

title: Latch
summary: Beacon Four resonance-locks into the corridor and stops obeying shutdown commands. Inside, Lantern Two's mapped exit shifts even though the cutter has not changed course.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — CLOSE Beacon Four's physical struts vibrating under a contained violet-white resonance, not exploding.
Panel 2 — SYSTEMS: shutdown command returns as accepted, but power draw stays high.
Panel 3 — MEDIUM Anik looks up sharply from the hardware telemetry.
Panel 4 — COCKPIT POV: the apparent exit and Beacon Six slide sideways relative to the inertial vector.
Panel 5 — CLOSE Rhea already issuing the abort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Abort the transit. Bring them home.

title: Do Not Fly at the Picture
summary: Lantern Two can see Glass Horizon, but flying toward the apparent ship increases measured separation. Mira stops Kess from chasing the visual exit and rebuilds the route from inertial history.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — COCKPIT POV: Glass Horizon appears clearly ahead, framed by the corridor opening.
Panel 2 — INSERT: distance increases while the ship appears larger.
Panel 3 — Kess begins a correction toward the image.
Panel 4 — Mira firmly calls the hold and brings up the untouched inertial breadcrumb trace.
Panel 5 — EXTERIOR: Lantern Two turns away from the visible Glass Horizon, an unnerving but controlled choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Give me the path we actually flew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Lantern Two, Glass Horizon. We trust your inertial.

title: Darken It in Order
summary: Anik realizes the beacon chain is feeding the resonance in sequence. A simultaneous shutdown would leave Beacon Four latched; the crew must collapse their own artificial stabilization in the reverse order it propagated.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE lab/system view with correction spikes stepping beacon to beacon.
Panel 2 — Anik draws a simple physical sequence across six hardware indicators with his finger.
Panel 3 — Olan sees that the growing stability was stored coupling, not free safety.
Panel 4 — Rhea asks for the operational instruction.
Panel 5 — Anik sends the first shutdown to Beacon Six.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: Darken the chain backward. Six to One. Let the fold shed us.

title: Ugly Is Honest
summary: As the beacons go dark in sequence, the corridor becomes noisy and visually unstable again. That ugliness restores agreement between independent measurements and gives Lantern Two a trustworthy way out.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — EXTERIOR/ABSTRACTED PHYSICAL VIEW. Beacon Six goes dark; subtle distortion relaxes rather than detonates.
Panel 2 — COCKPIT instruments flicker with noisier but mutually consistent ranges.
Panel 3 — Mira smiles for the first time because the disagreement is shrinking even as the ride worsens.
Panel 4 — Kess hand-flies the inertial breadcrumb path through a rougher corridor.
Panel 5 — COMMS from Anik as Beacon Four finally drops out of resonance.

title: Home Vector
summary: With the artificial field gone, Lantern Two follows its inertial history through the last unstable segment and re-emerges beside Glass Horizon.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — COCKPIT: physical vibration, imperfect stars, and a clean inertial home vector.
Panel 2 — WIDE exterior as Lantern Two emerges off-axis from the dark gap, much farther from the apparent exit than the crew had seen.
Panel 3 — Glass Horizon launches a tether drone that locks onto the cutter after emergence.
Panel 4 — CLOSE Kess finally allowing herself to breathe.
Panel 5 — BRIDGE/LAB reaction: no cheering spectacle, just quiet relief and immediate data capture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Visual contact. You are clear of the fold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kess Darrow
dialogueInline.text: Next time we send the expensive probe.

title: What the Data Permits
summary: The full team reconstructs the failure. The candidate can be made temporarily calm for light use, but repeated traffic increases beacon correction until the stabilization itself changes the route.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE debrief around the physical route table, cutter crew still in flight gear.
Panel 2 — Olan overlays transit count against correction load and shows the rising curve.
Panel 3 — Anik points to the latch point where the system stops being passive support.
Panel 4 — Pia translates the physics into certification language.
Panel 5 — Rhea asks the only question that matters for the map.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dr. Olan Crewe
dialogueInline.text: One ship can cross it cleanly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Anik Rell
dialogueInline.text: Then the next ship costs more correction. Then the next.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Tann
dialogueInline.text: Until the beacons become part of the geometry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: It is not a public route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Captain Rhea Solenne
dialogueInline.text: Can we make green mean safe?

title: Leave It Blank
summary: Pia archives the complete observation while removing the candidate from the public-route layer. Glass Horizon leaves the Aurin Rift with more knowledge and one intentionally blank space on the map.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — CLOSE Pia saving the full raw survey package into archive storage.
Panel 2 — ROUTE TABLE: the violet candidate line disappears from the public layer; nearby certified green lanes remain.
Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT Olan watching the line vanish, disappointed but not defeated.
Panel 4 — Rhea beside Pia at the map, the blank region between established routes visible.
Panel 5 — FINAL WIDE EXTERIOR. Glass Horizon turns away from the dark opening toward another unresolved part of the Aurin Belt; no beacon inside the candidate corridor is green.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: Raw survey preserved. Failure sequence preserved. Candidate rejected.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pia Oris
dialogueInline.text: We found why it is not a route.

title: Next — Echo Rescue
settingText: A dark Glass Horizon communications watch station after shift change. One small waveform hangs in otherwise empty space. Beyond the window, distant stars and a few cold survey lights. Do not show the source ship, survivors, anomaly solution or any literal ghost imagery.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser for the next Glass Horizon problem: a distress signal whose timestamp predates the people receiving it.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED TEASER. Quiet, sparse composition. Mira is small at the watch station while one impossible old distress waveform repeats. Reserve negative space for exact teaser copy.
LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat CAPTION and SYSTEM text as designed teaser typography. No invented explanatory text, coordinates, ship names or solution clues.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The ship that sent it was lost before Mira Tann was born.

directionInline.text: Tease the next scientific mystery without supernaturalizing it. The signal may be strange, but the page should not imply ghosts, monsters or magic.
Interior teaser page, not a cover. Preserve the established Glass Horizon workmanlike survey aesthetic.
